Synopsis:
Asian wheat importers are pivoting away from Black Sea supplies toward Australian and Argentine wheat following drone strikes and attacks on Ukrainian port infrastructure, notably ADM's Odesa terminal. At least 500k mt of alternative wheat has been secured at a significant premium ($310-330/t vs $260-280/t for Black Sea). Around 2.0-2.5 mmt of Black Sea wheat booked for July-September shipment faces delivery uncertainty. CBOT wheat futures have surged ~35% since late June, hitting a 3.5-year high. Some buyers are resorting to container shipments to manage price exposure and cover immediate needs.
